content.text: {"primary_meaning":"The four winds most commonly symbolize the four quarters or cardinal directions of the world and, by extension, worldwide extent, totality, or universality.","primary_basis":["Jeremiah 49:36 — four winds are brought from the four quarters of heaven, scattering Elam in every direction.","Ezekiel 37:9 — breath is summoned from the four winds, indicating every direction or the full compass of heaven.","Daniel 8:8; 11:4 — kingdoms or powers are divided toward the four winds of heaven, meaning the various regions of the world.","Zechariah 2:6 — Israel is scattered as the four winds of heaven, expressing widespread dispersion.","Matthew 24:31 and Mark 13:27 — the elect are gathered from the four winds, explicitly extending from one end of heaven or earth to the other.","Revelation 7:1 — four winds are positioned at the four corners of the earth, conveying comprehensive worldwide reach."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Forces or instruments of divine judgment, upheaval, or destruction operating throughout the world.","basis":["Jeremiah 49:36 associates the winds with conquest and scattering.","Daniel 7:2 depicts the four winds stirring the great sea before the emergence of the beasts.","Revelation 7:1-3 portrays the winds as harmful forces restrained until God's servants are sealed."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Heavenly spirits, angelic powers, or divine agents associated with the four regions of heaven.","basis":["Zechariah 6:5 can be translated as either the 'four spirits' or 'four winds' of heaven and identifies them with the four chariots going out from God's presence.","Revelation 7:1 links four angels with control over the four winds."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"The life-giving breath or Spirit of God summoned in its fullness.","basis":["Ezekiel 37:9-14 uses the same Hebrew word for wind, breath, and spirit; the breath from the four winds revives the dry bones."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Specific political kingdoms or historical powers.","basis":["Daniel 8:8 and 11:4 connect the four winds with the territorial division of kingdoms, leading some interpreters to identify them with particular political regions or successor powers.","Daniel 7:2 has sometimes encouraged historical identifications of the winds themselves, although the beasts, rather than the winds, are explicitly interpreted as kingdoms."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad consensus that the number four primarily marks the whole compass of the earth or heavens. The term's more specific function is context-dependent: it can denote worldwide dispersion or gathering, destructive judgment, heavenly agency, or life-giving breath. Thus, the general symbolism is settled, while the identity and action of the winds in individual passages are not always settled."}
